sites.name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge

sites.why: Best long-term illumination near the pole; Blue Origin Blue Moon MK1 'Endurance' target (NET early 2027, as of Nov 2026).

sites.name: Shackleton rim
sites.source: PGDA product 78 Site04 ROI (largest avg-illumination>70% region; PS x=-2812.5, y=-6647.5 m)

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.source: PGDA product 78 Site07 ROI (largest avg-illumination>70% region; PS x=30062.5, y=-20107.5 m)
sites.why: Chang'e-7 target region (launch slipped to 2027, as of Nov 2026).

sites.name: de Gerlache rim
sites.source: PGDA product 78 Site11 ROI (largest avg-illumination>70% region; PS x=-37542.5, y=14882.5 m)
sites.why: Artemis IV candidate region (de Gerlache Rim 2), as of Nov 2026.

sites.name: Malapert massif (summit)
sites.source: PGDA product 78 Site23: highest DEM point in the tile (5174 m)
sites.why: Earth almost always in view; Artemis candidate region.

sites.name: Mons Mouton (IM-2 landing site)
sites.source: Intuitive Machines IM-2 landing site (6 Mar 2025)
sites.why: IM-2 landed tipped over and ran about 12 h 45 min before its power ran out; Artemis candidate region.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1 (high point)
sites.source: PGDA product 78 Site06: highest DEM point in the tile (6800 m)

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti point)
sites.why: 'Near south pole' contrast: far from the polar DEMs, smooth-sphere horizon.

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.why: Equatorial contrast: the Sun climbs high and Earth hangs almost still.
